- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and prices are trending up, model often overcorrects; expect downward correction in next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 30d), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 7–14 days.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often ignores it; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day moving average.
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows volatility or divergence, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 10 days.
- If sentiment history includes 2+ consecutive 0.00 values, model tends to underestimate; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5 days), model often fails to anticipate; adjust downward bias by 3–5% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history includes 0.50 or higher, model often overestimates; apply downward correction of 2–4% for next 7 days.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong upward momentum, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is 0.00 and true outcome is rising, model often underestimates; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast.
